figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of the proposed system. (A) Conventional wired setup, in which a mouse with a Mini-Amp-64 headstage records PC activity through an amplifier, filter, and ADC. (B) Extracellular PC recording containing simple spikes (SSs) and complex spikes (CSs). (C) On-device spike detection and classification. (D) Output stored as sample index and spike type instead of raw data. (E) The two SNN classifiers: ConvSNN processes the full 57-value window as a fixed input over eight timesteps, while StreamSNN processes one waveform value per timestep through LIF neurons with learned time constants, fixed synaptic delays, and adaptive-threshold (ALIF) neurons.

Fig. 2. NEO-based spike detection and waveform extraction. Each detection defines a window spanning 30 samples before and 197 samples after the trough, reduced to 57 input values by four-sample averaging. Right: Functional mapping of ConvSNN onto the EFM32PG28 Cortex-M33 and MVP.
